Commentary.Commentary: West Indies have been made to toil hard for almost 6 sessions and had no answer how to deal with the hosts. They have their backs against the wall and will have to bat out of their skins if they are to give a fight. Will they be able to do so? Or will the Pakistani bowlers clean them up and enforce the follow-on? It remains to be seen. Join us in a bit for the Windies' reply...

Today, it was no different, Shafiq got out but not before scoring a fifty. Babar Azam then walked in and registered a fifty on debut. Azhar Ali was still out there and was looking rock solid ever since he came out to bat. Though he got a reprieve when he was batting on 190, but apart from that he was fluent throughout and did make the tourists pay for the same. Misbah-ul-Haq came out to bat just at the stroke of supper and once Ali drilled one to the fence and got the triple ton, he said he has had enough.

Pakistan were waiting for Azhar Ali's triple ton and the moment he did so, they have DECLARED the innings with a mammoth score of 579/3! This is some batting, 400th Test for Pakistan and boy, they have been absolutely brilliant with the willow. Literally whoever came in, reaped huge dividends from this wicket which is really, really good to bat on. Ali and Aslam added a marathon 215 for the first wicket and once the latter got out, Asad Shafiq saw off the day yesterday along with Ali.

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan doing the pitch report reckons that there is nothing much to worry for the batsmen. He adds that the pitch will remain on the slower side. Bazid wants the West Indian bowlers to bowl at the right pace to trouble the hosts.

West Indies were far from ideal with the ball and will hope to put in a better performance today. Roston Chase fared a lot better than Devendra Bishoo and one expects a lot more bowling from the spinners. Let's hope for a better contest today.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of Day 2 of the first ever D/N Test at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, Dubai. Pakistan are sitting right on top and will want to continue their good work with the bat. They have looked untroubled and one would hope West Indies will put up a good show today when they come out to bowl.
....DAY 2....SESSION 1....

West Indies lacked control and will want to put in a better performance tomorrow to keep their team in the game. Pakistan on the other hand, have a platform and could post a huge score on the board with a lot of batting left. It was quite a one-sided affair today, let's hope we see a lot better contest tomorrow. Do join us for all the action from Day 2. Take care and cheers!

Playing his 50th Test, Ali looked in superb touch and will want to bat on and register a big score. He and Shafiq have shared a good stand so far. This could be a typical UAE Test where the first two days are normally dominated by the bat followed by spinners coming to the fore. It's a good pitch to bat on and Pakistan will want to ensure they make the most of it.

A day dominated by Pakistan! Been a grinding first day of Test cricket. The hosts have finished well on a good batting strip after winning the toss. Their openers laid the platform with a brilliant 215-run stand. Both of them were tested at times but West Indies were not consistent to induce enough false strokes. The only wicket to fall was when Aslam dragged one onto his stumps on 90. Azhar Ali did not miss out like Aslam and ensured he got to his ton, his 11th one in Test cricket.
Floated full ball outside off, Ali lunges, takes his front leg right to the pitch of the ball and defends it solidly. STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flatter and shorter outside off, Ali goes for the cut off the back foot but ends up mistiming it towards short cover.

Nervy moment for Azhar! Tossed up ball outside off, Ali shuffles across the stumps and tries to work on the leg side but misses as it spins back in a shade. It pops out of his pads and goes behind to the slip region.

Welcome back for the final session of play. Pakistan are sitting in firm control of the game for now. The Pakistan openers have been troubled at times but the inconsistency has not helped West Indies. Sami Aslam and Azhar Ali are out to continue batting. West Indies begin the final session with Devendra Bishoo. Here we go...
DAY 1....SESSION 3....

The West Indian bowlers tried hard but without any success. The short-ball tactics against Sami Aslam was adopted but it was negotiated safely by the southpaw. Roston Chase impressed in his spell as he got good drift and turn along with some extra bounce. However, he didn't get much support from the other end. Devendra Bishoo is getting turn but he too has not looked threatening. 35 overs are still left in the last session, let's see how it pans out. Join us in a short while...

Another session bossed by Pakistan! They didn't run away with the game in terms of scoring briskly but did well to keep West Indies waiting for wickets. Both the openers once again batted with a lot of maturity and mixed caution with aggression in their approach.
Goes round the wicket to Aslam. Bowls it on the pads, Aslam works it through backward square leg for a single. That is the end of another dominating session for Pakistan. SUPPER, DAY 1!

But the umpire feels it's bat first and hence shakes his head. Jason Holder goes for the review after having a chat with his keeper and bowler. The replays show it's touch and go. The ball has hit the pad and Sami's gloves at the same point. 50-50 call. Now comes the Hawk Eye and it shows that the ball is going on to miss the leg stump. Sami survives a close call. West Indies have lost both their reviews now.
Shout for an lbw. Not given. Jason Holder takes his keeper and bowler's word and goes for the review.

DAY 1....SESSION 2....

West Indies kept the runs down at first but were not consistent with their lines and lengths. They will know if they do not strike early post-Tea, it could be a long, long evening for them. Do join us in a while for the second session of play.

PAKISTAN'S SESSION - Overs 27, Runs 81/0 - A typical first session of any Test match. Openers being reluctant to play their shots at the start and rightly so too. West Indies started in meandering fashion. Once both the openers settled, the runs began to flow for Pakistan. Both Aslam and Ali have looked untroubled so far and will want to continue their good work.

Slow loopy ball around off, angling in, Sami Aslam gets on the front foot and defends it to the off side.
Flicks a full ball just wide of mid on and crosses for a quick single.
Flighted ball outside off, Azhar gets down the track and defends it close to his front pad.
Holder comes from around the wicket and angles in a full ball on off, Sami defends it off his front foot to short cover.
Lands it full around middle and off, shaping away a touch, Sami draws forward in defense.
Too full in length and outside off, Aslam gets forward, opens the face of the bat and squeezes it through backward point for a couple of runs.
Pitches it full and around off, Aslam gets forward and defends it watchfully.
Fuller in length around middle and leg, Aslam gets on the front foot and defends it to the leg side.
Back of a length ball around middle and leg, Sami stands back and turns it through backward square leg for a couple of runs.

Back of a length outside off, Aslam rides the bounce and taps it towards covers.

Short of a good length outside off, pushed towards gully by Aslam.
DRINKS BREAK!
On a length on off, Azhar defends it off the inside half of the bat towards the on side.
FOUR! DEFT! Back of a length on off, Azhar gets across and clips it fine past the keeper for a boundary.

FOUR! CHANCE GOES MISSING! A touch short outside off, Azhar attempts to flash it hard but it is not in control of it. The ball goes through the hands of the gully fielder. Johnson, the fielder did not spot the ball there. A chance goes down for West Indies.
On a length outside off, Azhar defends it with his bat and pad together.
Similar length, slightly short outside off, Azhar pushes it into the off side.
Good length on off, Azhar punches it towards covers.
Back of a length on middle, Sami gets across and defends it back down the wicket towards mid-wicket.
Fuller outside off, Aslam pushes it through covers but not in the gap.
On a fuller length on middle, Aslam fends it towards the on side.
Aslam defends this one from his crease.
Angled in on a length outside off, Aslam comes forward and defends it.
Back of a length on off, Sami defends it off the inside half of the bat onto his pads. Sami was not quite in the right position to play that one.
Full again outside off, Azhar looks to drive but does not time it well enough.

Pitched up outside off, Aslam comes forward and pushes it to covers and takes a single.
Back of a length outside off, Aslam stands tall and places it towards gully but not for any runs.

Good length on middle and leg, Sami tucks it nicely through square leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length on middle, Azhar gets across and taps it towards the on side.
Good length outside off, Azhar shoulders his arms to it.
Slanted on the pads, Aslam looks to work it through fine leg but does not connect with his bat. The ball goes off his pads and rolls towards square leg for a leg bye.
Holder goes round the wicket and bowls it on a length, Aslam defends this one off his back foot.
Fuller on middle, Ali leans across and clips it wide of mid on for a single.
Good length outside off, Azhar punches it towards covers off his crease.
On the stumps from Cummins, Aslam gets across and turns it towards the on side.
This one is played towards point by Aslam.
Aslam defends it off his crease.
Back of a length on middle, Sami rises with the bounce and keeps it down.
Shorter in length outside off, Aslam is right forward and blocks it.
Fuller outside off, Aslam comes forward and defends it.
Change of ends for Cummins.
Fuller in length and Ali responds with a drive but does not get it past the bowler.
Good length on off, Azhar pushes it towards covers.
Good length outside off, left alone by Azhar.
On a length outside off, pushed into the off side by Azhar but not for any runs.
Back of a length on the pads, tucked down to fine leg for a single.
Good length on off, Aslam taps it towards the on side off his crease.

Pitched up outside off, Azhar is forward and defends it.

Angled in fuller on off, Azhar drives it nicely down the ground but too straight for him as the ball crashes into the stumps at the non-striker's end.
On a length on the stumps, Ali defends it.
Fuller outside off again, Aslam squirts it through covers but not in the gap.

Fuller outside off, Azhar comes forward and pushes it to covers off his crease.

Length outside off, Aslam is happy to let it go through.
Shorter in length on middle, worked behind square leg for a couple of runs by Aslam.
Fuller in length on the stumps, Aslam comes forward and defends it towards the on side.

Fuller outside off, Azhar comes forward and pushes it through covers for a couple of runs.

Another length ball but not directed well, Aslam again fails to work it through. Aslam got out trying to clip deliveries on his pads in the last series against England and it seems West Indies have done their homework on him.

MIGUEL CUMMINS to bowl from the other end.

Game time! The Pakistan openers are out to bat. SAMI ASLAM and AZHAR ALI are out in the middle. SHANNON GABRIEL has the new PINK ball in his hands. The first ever D/N Test in Asia is about to begin. Here we go...
PAKISTAN XI - Sami Aslam, Azhar Ali, Babar Azam(debut), Misbah-ul-Haq(c), Asad Shafiq, Sarfraz Ahmed(wk), Mohammad Nawaz(debut), Wahab Riaz, Yasir Shah, Mohammad Amir, Sohail Khan.
WEST INDIES XI - Kraigg Brathwaite, Leon Johnson, Darren Bravo, Marlon Samuels, Jermaine Blackwood, Roston Chase, Shane Dowrich(wk), Jason Holder(c), Devendra Bishoo, Miguel Cummins, Shannon Gabriel.

Jason Holder states that they have had a good time preparing for the Tests and acclimatizing should not be a worry for them. Hopes the team can adjust quickly and get into the groove. Is confident of putting a good show and making sure they capitalize on the opportunities. We'll have the teams for you in a bit.

TOSS - Misbah-ul-Haq has won the toss and PAKISTAN WILL BAT! Interestingly it is the 17th time in a row that a non-Asian captain has lost the toss in a Test in Asia.  Misbah reckons it is a good batting wicket. He is proud of a being part of the 400th Test for Pakistan. He wants his players to not worry too much about the pink ball and just see the ball and play normally. Babar Azam and Mohammad Nawaz are making their Test debut.

PITCH REPORT - The pitch looks to be a good one for batting. Bazid Khan doing the pitch report reckons it is a dry deck and will assist the spinners and the pink ball will move around under lights. There isn't a visible covering of grass on the surface and that could dictate how things pan out.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of the first ever D/N Test match between Pakistan and West Indies from the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, Dubai. It is a milestone game for Pakistan as well, they are playing their 400th Test and will be hoping to make it a memorable one. The Test team of Pakistan is coming off an impressive performance in England and having had the wood over West Indies so far, they once again start as favorites for sure. West Indies had a forgetful time in ODIs and T20Is and will hope for a better time in whites.
